metadata.title: Engineering Information Residuality Stress Test
metadata.description: Five proposed business-context stress tests; these are design thought experiments and not reported Assai incidents.
metadata.naiveArchitecture: Documents are uploaded, indexed and exchanged; successful delivery is treated as accepted information, and source availability and permissions are assumed stable.
metadata.residualArchitecture: Controlled records, derived context and change-completion obligations have explicit authority. Source permissions, freshness, baseline conflicts, portable custody and migration reconciliation are observable and subject to accountable acceptance.
metadata.note: All residues are candidates for implementation validation. No survived-incident claims or forecasts are made.

stressors.name: A revoked supplier retains indexed engineering information
stressors.detection: A revoked-supplier test still returns a document snippet or asset relationship.
stressors.attractor: A customer suspends collaboration because source permissions are not enforced throughout derived discovery.
stressors.businessReaction: Invalidate derived access, contain affected scope, preserve incident evidence and verify all relevant source/project revocation paths before restoring sharing.
stressors.residue: Revocation-aware discovery, bounded source scopes and repeated permission acceptance checks become required delivery controls.

stressors.name: A source outage makes operating context silently stale
stressors.detection: Freshness thresholds are exceeded while the context viewer appears healthy.
stressors.attractor: Maintenance preparation cannot distinguish current source state from cached context and the asset owner withdraws trust.
stressors.businessReaction: Expose degraded source state, stop claiming currency, reconcile failed exchange items and require source-owner verification of restoration.
stressors.residue: Per-source freshness contracts, visible degraded states and reconciled recovery evidence persist across connectors.

stressors.name: Two modification projects return conflicting master changes
stressors.detection: Two approved copies depend on different master baselines or alter the same equipment documentation.
stressors.attractor: Operations needs one defensible accepted record while both contractors claim their design is complete.
stressors.businessReaction: Hold incorporation, preserve both lineages, appoint the engineering decision owner and verify all required downstream updates after conflict resolution.
stressors.residue: Explicit master baselines and verified change obligations remain durable platform concepts.

stressors.name: A contract ends before the operating asset can leave the platform
stressors.detection: A renewal decision exposes missing export rights, incomplete lineage or an unusable reconstruction sample.
stressors.attractor: The asset owner must preserve information custody for ongoing operations despite supplier or commercial change.
stressors.businessReaction: Agree the retained evidence set, reconcile an export and independently reconstruct critical tag/document/approval relationships before service termination.
stressors.residue: Documented export contracts and recurring reconstruction exercises become part of service acceptance.

stressors.name: A migration rehearsal exposes missing engineering history
stressors.detection: Input-to-output reconciliation reveals unexplained record differences and broken predecessor references.
stressors.attractor: A go-live deadline conflicts with the receiving organization accepting a reliable operating information set.
stressors.businessReaction: Pause affected scope, quarantine malformed records, rehearse corrections and rollback, and require named customer acceptance of every unresolved exception.
stressors.residue: Repeatable mappings, complete reconciliation and explicit cutover acceptance persist beyond the initial implementation.
